title: Normalized blowup finality over a locally Noetherian base
statement: Let $S$ be a reduced locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $J\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent] whose zero scheme is nowhere dense (its complement meets every irreducible component densely). Write $b:W=\operatorname{Bl}_J S\to S$ for its ordinary blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] and $p:N=W^\nu\to S$ for its componentwise normalization followed by $b$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Then $W$ is reduced and locally Noetherian, $b$ is proper and surjective [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and $b$ gives a bijection on component generic points with isomorphic residue fields [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-residue-field]. The scheme $N$ is normal (all its local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]); $p$ is surjective and gives the same bijection on generic points and generic residue fields. The extended ideal $J\mathcal O_N$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is an invertible ideal, meaning it is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. If $g:Z\to S$ is any morphism from a normal scheme which takes each component generic point to a component generic point of $S$, and $J\mathcal O_Z$ is an invertible ideal, there is a unique $S$-morphism $Z\to N$. No characteristic, finite-type-over-a-field, excellence, or finiteness-of-normalization hypothesis is imposed. In particular $N$ itself is not assumed locally Noetherian. Empty schemes and the unit ideal are allowed.

source.place: VIII 2.2.1--2.2.4(i), printed p.90. Ordinary blowup inputs: Stacks Tags 0808 (divisors.tex, lemma-blow-up-reduced-scheme), 0BFM (lemma-blow-up-and-irreducible-components), 0806 (lemma-universal-property-blowing-up); normalization inputs: 035Q (morphisms.tex, lemma-normalization-normal).

proof.text: Regard schemes as their representable algebraic spaces [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Apply the scheme case explicitly included in [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] to $J$: $b$ is proper, restricts to an isomorphism $b^{-1}U\to U$ for $U=S\setminus V(J)$, and $J\mathcal O_W$ is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. These generators can be taken Zariski-locally: for an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with ideal $K$, the same statement covers $b^{-1}\operatorname{Spec}R$ by the open charts $\operatorname{Spec}R[K/a]$, $a\in K$, and there $K\,R[K/a]=aR[K/a]$ since $x=a\cdot(x/a)$; as $R[K/a]$ is a subring of $R_a$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], in which $a$ is a unit, $a$ is a nonzerodivisor on it. The same cited statement identifies $b^{-1}V$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{J|_V}V$ for every affine open $V\subset S$. Choose a Noetherian affine cover of $S$ [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Its members are reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and the restricted ideals are coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], which identifies coherence with quasi-coherence of finite type on a locally Noetherian scheme. Apply [lem-per-reduced-noetherian-blowup-geometry] on each member: these inverse images are reduced and Noetherian. They cover $W$, so its local rings are reduced and it has a Noetherian affine cover. Thus $W$ is reduced and locally Noetherian. Properness also says that the underlying map $b$ is closed [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tags 0808 (lemma-blow-up-reduced-scheme), 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor), 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective); scheme cases of spaces-divisors.tex Tags 085S, 085T, 085Z.

proof.text: No generic point of $W$ belongs to $V(J\mathcal O_W)$. Indeed on an affine open where this ideal is $(a)$, the ring is reduced and $a$ is a nonzerodivisor; [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-zerodivisors-union-minimal-primes] puts $a$ outside every minimal prime, which represents a component generic point by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. Every component has a unique generic point [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. For an open containing all component generic points, its components are precisely the intersections with the ambient components: injection and irreducibility are [lem-sc-components-open-injection]; for surjection, contain any component of the open in an ambient component by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] and use maximality. Thus the isomorphism $b^{-1}U\simeq U$ bijects component generic points of $W$ and $S$, since both opens contain all those points. It identifies their local rings and hence residue fields. The closed set $b(W)$ contains $U$, which is dense in every component of $S$; therefore $b(W)=S$. This proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0BFM (lemma-blow-up-and-irreducible-components), proof; reduced-ring argument and the open-component correspondence written explicitly.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-componentwise-normalization-properties](1) to the locally Noetherian scheme $W$. It says that $N=W^
u$ is normal, $
u:N	o W$ is surjective, and it bijects component generic points; its fibre over each such point $\xi$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ over that field. In particular the corresponding generic residue fields are identical. Composing with the surjectivity and generic-point/residue-field bijections of Step 2 gives exactly the assertions about $p=b
u$. For later uses note also that every quasi-compact open $V$ of $W$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], hence Noetherian by the locally Noetherian plus quasi-compact convention, and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. This verifies the target hypothesis of both normalization tools used below; it places no Noetherian assumption on $N$.

source.place: Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal)(1),(2), with the generic fibre specified in the cited normalization-properties statement.

proof.text: Refine the Cartier-generator cover from Step 1 to affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset W$ with $J\mathcal O_W|_V=(a)$ and $a$ a nonzerodivisor. By [lem-sfb-normalization-affine-total-fractions], $\nu^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline A$ with $\overline A\subset Q(A)$ and structural map $a\mapsto a/1$. In $Q(A)$ this element is a unit, so multiplication by $a$ is injective on its subring $\overline A$. The extended ideal there is $(a)\overline A$: extension is generated by images, and successive extensions give the same ideal as the composite ring map [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Thus these opens give nonzerodivisor generators of $J\mathcal O_N$, exactly the invertible-ideal convention in the statement [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. This argument uses no flatness of normalization.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), affine total-fraction form; divisors.tex Tag 02OS. Explicit multiplication calculation.

proof.text: Let $g:Z\to S$ satisfy the hypotheses. The representable case of [lem-sfb-space-blowup-universal-property] gives a unique $u:Z\to W$ with $bu=g$, since $J\mathcal O_Z$ has Zariski-local nonzerodivisor generators, which stay nonzerodivisors on etale charts because etale morphisms are flat [def-weil-etale-morphism] and tensoring the injection $a\cdot$ with a flat algebra keeps it injective, and on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C$ both the image ideal of the space statement and the extended ideal equal $JC$. Here schemes are regarded as the representables of [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]; the conversion back to schemes is explicit: a natural transformation $h_Z\to h_W$ is composition with its value on $\operatorname{id}_Z$, by naturality on each test morphism $T\to Z$. Thus uniqueness is uniqueness of actual scheme maps. If $\zeta$ is any component generic point of $Z$, $g(\zeta)$ is a component generic point of $S$ and belongs to $U$. Since $b^{-1}U\to U$ is an isomorphism and Step 2 bijects generic points, $u(\zeta)$ is the corresponding component generic point of $W$. For $C=\overline{\{\zeta\}}$, continuity gives $u(C)\subseteq\overline{\{u(\zeta)\}}$; because $u(\zeta)\in u(C)$, taking closures gives equality. Each component of $Z$ therefore dominates a component of $W$.

source.place: Tag 085U (lemma-universal-property-blowing-up), scheme case, equivalently divisors.tex Tag 0806; ILO VIII Proposition 2.2.4(i), ordinary-blowup factor.

proof.text:
The normality of $Z$, the component dominance in Step 5, and the finite-component condition verified in Step 3 allow [lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift] to be applied to $u:Z	o W$. It gives a unique $h:Z	o N$ with $
u h=u$, hence $ph=g$. If $h_1,h_2:Z	o N$ are any $S$-morphisms, the uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-space-blowup-universal-property] gives $
u h_1=u=
u h_2$. The uniqueness clause of the normalization lifting theorem then gives $h_1=h_2$. Neither tool requires $Z$ to be quasi-compact or locally Noetherian. All constructions and arguments include the empty scheme; when $J=\mathcal O_S$ one has $U=S$, $W=S$, and the argument is exactly the normalization mapping property. No characteristic or excellence hypothesis has entered.
